messages:
PagerBot: [ALERT] High router fallback rate detected for dedicated-pool 'eu-west-2-ded-42' — 5m error-rate 18% :rotating_light:
alex.k: seeing same in dashboards, routing fallback spikes, a bunch of traffic is getting dropped into the fallback loop. Paging oncall.
maya.s: jumping in, oncall for infra today. checking metrics & recent config changes. any deploys?
josh.r: no deploys in last 40m from runtime. I can check router policy recent pushes.
PagerBot: incident created INC-236001 (auto) — severity: page; paged: @oncall-eng-infra.
alex.k: timeline: ~2360012200 first spike, escalated now. impact: elevated 5xx and long tail latencies for customers on dedicated pools in eu-west-2.
lina.ps: CS notes: 1 customer reported throttled requests at 13:12 CET, says errors returned as 503. Ticket #5421.
maya.s: looking at autoscaler metrics — dedicated pool 'ded-42' shows a sudden drop in active replicas triggered by the autoscaler at 2360012100, but traffic (qps) increased. that doesn't add up.
josh.r: pulling router debug: router is scoring variants by metric polarity and appears to have inverted the capacity signal. we use the metric name 'pool_available_capacity_pct' in the fallback policy; graph shows negative correlation.
alex.k: meaning the router thinks capacity is high when it's low?
maya.s: exactly — metric ingestion pipeline recently had unit-change behavior: exporter reported free GPUs as negative on overflow and the policy threshold comparator flipped outcome.
ben.e: who pushed the metrics exporter change? I saw a PR merged earlier today that touched node-exporter -> metrics-normalizer.
josh.r: PR 876 by infra-tooling altered the gauge normalization; it changed sign for some cumulative counters under heavy memory pressure.
PagerBot: @deploy-bot pushed infra-tooling PR 876 at 2360010005 (build #4092).
maya.s: immediate plan: 1) disable automatic fallback policy for eu-west-2 routing group (override to prefer direct pool routing) 2) set pool ded-42 to force-scale=+2 manual to avoid shrink 3) pin router to stable variant 1.4.3 (no canary) 4) roll back metrics-normalizer or patch to correct sign.
alex.k: agree. Josh — can you apply the router override? Lina — can you update CS with a short blurb about degraded service and that engineering is investigating? Ben — can you revert the metrics-normalizer?
josh.r: executing override now: `POST /api/v1/router/overrides -d '{"scope":"eu-west-2","policy":"fallback","mode":"bypass"}'` 
[josh.r edits the router override]
josh.r: override accepted, fallback bypass active. routing should stop bouncing to fallback variants. watching for request success.
maya.s: manual scale command: `redwoodctl pool scale ded-42 --replicas 6 --reason "mitigation: autoscaler mis-signal"`
maya.s: scale applied, expected warm-up ~30s.
ben.e: rolling back infra-tooling PR 876 now. `git revert 876 && ./ci/run-lint && ./ci/deploy-metrics-normalizer --staged`
ben.e: revert deployed to staging, canarying revert to prod next minute.
PagerBot: [INFO] Revert deployment started for metrics-normalizer build #4094.
alex.k: watch for metric shape change — once normalizer fixed, autoscaler should stop mis-reading. we should not re-enable fallback policy until stable.
josh.r: router logs show immediate drop in fallback attempts after override; 5xx rate trending down from 18% -> 6% in 90s.
lina.ps: CS update posted: "Engineering investigating intermittent 503s for EU dedicated customers. Mitigation in progress; we're scaling capacity and applying a fix. We'll update within 30m." cc @cs-oncall
cs-oncall: acknowledged, will escalate to account contacts for affected customers.
maya.s: revert rolled to prod. confirming metric polarity: `metric:pool_available_capacity_pct` now returns expected 0..100 positive values again.
ben.e: pushed config change to add sign-checker to metrics-normalizer to catch future flips.
josh.r: autoscaler readout shows no further shrink triggers after metric corrected. gating autoscale and fallback off until next maintenance window.
alex.k: quick postmortem notes: root cause = metrics-normalizer change flipped sign on capacity gauge under overflow; fallback policy logic assumed monotonicity and ended up sending traffic to fallback variants while autoscaler simultaneously interpreted signal and scaled down -> caused transient blackholing. Contributing factor: no sign assertion in comparator.
maya.s: next actions: 1) add sign sanity check to critical metrics 2) require canary + alert for polarity changes 3) add temporary circuit-breaker: if fallback rate spikes >10% in 5m, set router to fail-open to direct to primary instead of fallback 4) schedule runbook update and postmortem.
alex.k: I'll draft customer-facing summary and coordinate with sales/CS on impacted accounts.
lina.ps: Customer-facing message draft ready, will share in #customer-updates for review.
PagerBot: Incident INC-236001 status: acknowledged -> mitigated. Postmortem requested.
ben.e: adding tags: autoscaler, routing, metrics, production, customer-impact.
josh.r: leaving logs and snippets in the incident doc: `/internal/incidents/INC-236001/logs` (link).
maya.s: handing off to oncall rotation for follow-ups — @alex.k staying as incident lead for postmortem. I'll update runbook changes in infra repo.
alex.k: thanks everyone. monitoring for 30m then clear. :white_check_mark:
